In the 2030s, most municipalities and national parks remained in the same or adjacent richness classes as at present, and differences between SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 were minor (Figure 7, Figure 8, Figure 9 and Figure 10). Although many are highly fragmented49 and dispersed across continents, especially in Africa, these tropical forests are the best candidates to act as climate refugia and are crucial to conservation efforts. Severe fragmentation will also influence temperature novelty as edge effects have been shown to reduce microclimatic temperature buffering up to 20 m into the interior51. It is paramount that distant wealth-related drivers of deforestation and degradation begin to be sufficiently addressed52 and that intact candidate refugia are urgently and vigorously protected, via legal protection53, carbon payments54 or empowering indigenous communities55.
